title: Roots Keep Growing in Winter
core_idea: Beneath cold winter ground, roots keep working slowly while nothing shows above; quiet seasons in our own lives may be doing hidden work too.
text: In early winter, a garden can look finished. The stems are brown, the soil is cold, and nothing seems to be happening at all. Yet beneath the surface, many roots keep growing slowly, reaching a little deeper, storing what they will need in spring. Nothing about it is visible. Nothing about it is wasted. Maybe some of our own seasons are like that. The weeks when you feel quiet and unproductive, when nothing new appears, may still be doing deep and patient work. So if your life feels like bare ground right now, be gentle with it. Not every kind of growth wants to be seen.
description: A calm reflection on winter roots, and the hidden growth that can happen in quiet seasons of life.
